role: Main-actor wrapper around one UIApplication.beginBackgroundTask assertion that guarantees endBackgroundTask is called exactly once, either by the work's own end() or by the expiration handler.
types: BackgroundTaskAssertion: class (@MainActor final) — owns one UIBackgroundTaskIdentifier

flags.text: There is no deinit that ends the task and the expiration handler captures self weakly; if an owner ever drops the object without calling end(), the handler's self?.end() is a no-op and iOS terminates the app at expiry. Both current callers use `defer { bgTask.end() }`, so this holds only by caller discipline.

units.does: Begins a named UIKit background task; the expiration handler (main thread, assumed MainActor) logs a warning via debugLog, runs the caller's onExpire (e.g. MorningProcessingService sets skipSleepWait) and then ends the assertion.
calls: closure:onExpire supplied by MorningProcessingService.processOvernightData (sets skipSleepWait = true) or the default no-op from WorkoutRecorder stop

flags.text: No test in EmuquTests references BackgroundTaskAssertion; the exactly-once end() contract (expiry then completion, or the reverse) that keeps iOS from killing the app is unverified.

units.does: Ends the background task if one is held and resets the identifier to .invalid; a second call is a no-op.
units.entry: Called by the owner's `defer` (MorningProcessingService.swift:197, WorkoutRecorder+Stop.swift:54) and by the iOS expiration handler installed in init.

branches.effect: true: return without calling UIKit; false: call endBackgroundTask and set .invalid.
